prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: transparent production game animation sprite atlas, 4 columns by 4 rows, 16 full-body poses.
Input image 1 is the existing adventurer identity and rendering style reference. Preserve his chestnut hair, teal tunic, cream sleeves, ochre scarf, brown belt, dark trousers, brown boots and approachable anime/chibi proportions. Create new directional drawings; do not reuse the original straight-front, pure-side, or straight-back views.
Primary request: the SAME simple adventurer walking in the FOUR DIAGONAL directions of a fixed orthographic fantasy RPG camera about 31 degrees above the ground. Every drawing uses a consistent slightly overhead view, with head top/shoulder tops visible. Each character faces the direction his feet travel.
Precise square regular atlas: exactly FOUR equal-height rows and FOUR equal-width columns, one complete isolated character per cell, same scale, foot baseline and center within each cell, generous fully transparent gutters. No labels or grid lines.
ROW 1 (all four cells): SOUTHEAST, walking toward the viewer and toward screen RIGHT, front-right THREE-QUARTER view. Face and tunic front visible, nose points diagonally lower-right, both eyes readable with farther eye smaller. NOT a straight-front or pure-side view.
ROW 2 (all four cells): SOUTHWEST, toward the viewer and screen LEFT, front-left THREE-QUARTER view. Face and tunic front visible, nose points diagonally lower-left. NOT a straight-front or pure-side view.
ROW 3 (all four cells): NORTHEAST, AWAY from viewer toward screen RIGHT, rear-right THREE-QUARTER view. Show back of head, back of teal tunic, far shoulder; at most a tiny cheek profile, NO front-facing eyes or belt buckle. Feet advance diagonally upper-right.
ROW 4 (all four cells): NORTHWEST, AWAY from viewer toward screen LEFT, rear-left THREE-QUARTER view. Show back of head and tunic; at most tiny cheek profile, NO front-facing eyes or belt buckle. Feet advance diagonally upper-left.
Columns in EVERY row are a coherent four-pose walk loop: 1 left leg forward/right back with opposite arm swing; 2 passing pose; 3 right leg forward/left back; 4 opposite passing pose. Keep the exact same facing throughout each row, same identity and proportions. Distinct alternating leg/arm poses, not static standing copies.
Clean hand-painted 2D anime sprite, modest detail, crisp restrained outlines and simple cel shading matching the reference. Same neutral light in every frame.
Constraints: genuinely transparent RGBA background, no ground or contact shadow, no scenery, no additional people, no weapons, no text, no captions, no watermark, no visible grid, no checkerboard baked into the pixels, no cropped hair/feet or overlapping cells. Critical: front-diagonal rows above and back-diagonal rows below, never switch a row to a cardinal facing.
revision_prompt:
Edit this sprite atlas only to improve the alternating walk cycle. Preserve the same character, identity, clothes, drawing style, all four diagonal row facings, exact 4x4 layout, scale and transparent background. Row1 southeast/front-right; row2 southwest/front-left; row3 northeast/back-right; row4 northwest/back-left.
Critical correction: currently several poses repeat the same leading leg. In EVERY row, keep column1 as the first contact pose, but draw column3 as the OPPOSITE contact pose: the leg that was behind in column1 must be clearly forward in column3, and the formerly forward leg must clearly be behind. Swap the arm swing too. Column2 and column4 must be opposite passing poses between those contacts. Keep all feet on a consistent baseline within the cells, same body size and ample padding. Head and torso keep the same diagonal facing throughout the entire row. Do not rotate toward a cardinal facing. Rear rows must show the character's back.
No other changes. No text, grids, floor, shadows, scenery or extra characters. Preserve real transparent alpha.
selection_note: All four diagonal rows authored: SE, SW, NE, NW. No mirrored directions. Inspect gait quality manually; the generated four-pose loop is prototype art, not a substitute for artist cleanup.
